result:
I fixed this: datasets with uneven nested lists of dictionaries now convert to an evaluation dataset without error. The new tests fail without the fix and pass with it.

**Cause.** When hashing an array whose items are themselves arrays, `_hash_array_like_obj_as_bytes` in `mlflow/data/evaluation_dataset.py` called `np.array(data.tolist())`, which forces the data into a rectangular 2D array. If the inner arrays have different lengths, NumPy raises `ValueError: ... inhomogeneous shape`. This happens with Hugging Face datasets when a column used as targets or predictions holds lists of dicts of varying length. I reproduced it that way with `from_huggingface(...).to_evaluation_dataset()`. Feature columns weren't affected because they're hashed cell by cell.

**Fix.** That branch now checks `_is_array_has_dict(data)` first. If the nested arrays contain dicts, it hashes the actual contents with the existing `_hash_array_of_dict_as_bytes` and skips the stacking step entirely.

**Existing hashes don't change.** For arrays of dicts that are all the same length, the old path stacked them into 2D and then ended up in `_hash_array_of_dict_as_bytes` anyway. Walking a 2D array row by row produces the same bytes as walking the original array of arrays, so those hashes stay the same. Any other data (no dicts) goes through the old code unchanged.

**Tests** (in `tests/evaluate/test_evaluation.py`):
- `test_gen_md5_for_arraylike_obj_with_ragged_nested_arrays_of_dicts` checks that uneven arrays of dicts hash without error and that different contents give different hashes. It also checks that equal-length data gives exactly the same hash as the old stack-into-2D method.
- `test_evaluation_dataset_with_ragged_nested_arrays_of_dicts_as_targets` builds an end-to-end `EvaluationDataset` using such a column as targets.

The existing MD5 and hash tests also pass. The one exception is `test_dataset_hash`, which errored during setup because its Spark fixture couldn't start Java (`JAVA_GATEWAY_EXITED`), so it didn't run here.
